subject: paediatrics
title: Neonatal Hypoglycaemia, Hypocalcaemia and Diabetic Mother

steps.tx: The most common metabolic derangement in the neonatal intensive care unit is **neonatal symptomatic hypoglycaemia**, defined as a plasma glucose concentration below forty to forty-five milligrams per deciliter. Because the developing brain relies almost exclusively on glucose oxidation for cellular metabolism, untreated hypoglycemia precipitates irreversible neuronal necrosis within the occipital and parietal cortices.
steps.say: Blood glucose below forty to forty-five milligrams per deciliter demands prompt correction to protect the brain.

rows: Depleted hepatic glycogen and adipose stores
Screen at 2 hours of life, then pre-feed every 3 to 4 hours
Screen within 1 hour of life, then every 2 to 3 hours
Serial monitoring during cooling and rewarming

steps.tx: Birth cuts off a glucose infusion the fetus never had to request. Once the cord is clamped, placental supply stops and blood glucose slides to a **physiological nadir** at one to two hours before glycogen breakdown and new glucose production take over. Babies with small stores, or insulin pushing the other way, fall through that dip into symptomatic hypoglycaemia, which is why screening targets exactly this window.
steps.say: After cord clamping, glucose dips to a nadir at one to two hours before glycogen breakdown takes over. Babies with poor stores or excess insulin fall furthest in that window.

vis.alt: Line graph of blood glucose falling after cord clamping to a low point at one to two hours, then rising as stores are mobilised.
vis.caption: Glucose transition after birth, from placental supply to glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, with the physiological nadir at one to two hours. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Clinical manifestations of neuroglycopenia include **jitteriness and fine tremors**, which must be distinguished from true epileptic seizures. Jitteriness is stimulus-sensitive, exhibits rapid alternating tremors without autonomic instability or gaze deviation, and ceases completely when the limb is gently held. In contrast, neonatal seizures are non-stimulus sensitive and persist despite passive limb restraint.
steps.say: Jitteriness stops when the limb is held, differentiating it from true neonatal epileptic seizures.

left.title: Neonatal Jitteriness
points: Stimulus sensitive (provoked by sound or touch)
Fine, rapid alternating tremor of extremities
Ceases immediately upon passive gentle limb flexion

right.title: Neonatal Seizures
points: Spontaneous, non-stimulus sensitive
Rhythmic clonic jerking with fast and slow phases
Persists unabated when limb is held by examiner

steps.tx: While that critical sample is drawn, the tremor at the cot still has to be read correctly. Neuroglycopenia produces **jitteriness and fine tremors**, which must be told apart from true epileptic seizures. Jitteriness is provoked by a stimulus, shows rapid alternating tremor without autonomic instability or gaze deviation, and stops completely when the limb is gently held. Neonatal seizures are not set off by a stimulus and continue despite passive restraint of the limb.
steps.say: Jitteriness from low glucose is triggered by a stimulus, shows fast tremor without gaze deviation or autonomic change, and stops when the limb is held. Neonatal seizures are not stimulus provoked and persist despite restraint. The limb holding test separates them while the critical blood sample is taken.

vis.alt: A diagnostic flowchart lists insulin, cortisol, growth hormone, free fatty acids, and ketone bodies to be drawn during persistent neonatal hypoglycaemia.
vis.caption: The critical sample is taken while glucose is still low and before treatment, so insulin, cortisol, growth hormone, free fatty acids, and ketones can be interpreted together. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Emergency management of symptomatic hypoglycemia requires an **immediate intravenous dextrose bolus** of two milliliters per kilogram of ten percent dextrose in water, delivering two hundred milligrams of glucose per kilogram. This is followed immediately by continuous maintenance infusion providing a glucose infusion rate of six to eight milligrams per kilogram per minute, titrated to maintain euglycemia.
steps.say: A bolus of two milliliters per kilogram of ten percent dextrose is followed by continuous glucose infusion.

rows: Rapidly restores plasma glucose above 50 mg/dL
Matches baseline endogenous hepatic glucose production
Increase GIR in steps up to 12 to 15 mg/kg/min

steps.tx: The prototype of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia is the **infant of a diabetic mother**. Maternal hyperglycemia drives transplacental glucose transfer, stimulating fetal pancreatic islet beta-cell hyperplasia. Fetal hyperinsulinemia promotes excessive glycogen and lipid synthesis, resulting in fetal macrosomia with birth weight exceeding four thousand grams, organomegaly, plethoric cushingoid facies, and severe rebound post-delivery hypoglycemia.
steps.say: Fetal hyperinsulinism drives macrosomia and causes severe rebound hypoglycemia once the cord is clamped.

left.title: Pedersen Hypothesis Cascade
points: Maternal hyperglycemia stimulates fetal pancreas
Fetal islet beta-cell hyperplasia
Hyperinsulinemia acts as primary anabolic growth factor

right.title: Neonatal Clinical Phenotype
points: Macrosomia with birth weight over 4000g
Plethoric round 'tomato-face' appearance
Visceromegaly (hepatosplenomegaly and cardiomegaly)

steps.tx: Cardiac evaluation in infants of diabetic mothers frequently reveals **transient asymmetric septal hypertrophy**. Fetal hyperinsulinemia stimulates excessive glycogen and fat deposition directly into the interventricular septum, narrowing the left ventricular outflow tract and producing functional subaortic stenosis with a harsh systolic ejection murmur that resolves spontaneously over two to four months.
steps.say: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy produces transient subaortic stenosis that resolves spontaneously.

rows: High insulin antagonizes cortisol on pneumocytes
Delayed surfactant synthesis despite mature dates

steps.tx: A highly specific congenital structural anomaly occurring almost exclusively in diabetic pregnancies is **caudal regression syndrome**, also termed sacral agenesis. Characterized by agenesis of the sacrum and lumbar spine with hypoplastic lower extremities in a fixed frog-leg position, it results from early teratogenic disruption of the caudal mesoderm before the seventh week of gestation.
steps.say: Caudal regression syndrome causes sacral agenesis and is pathognomonic of diabetic embryopathy.

left.title: Caudal Regression Features
points: Agenesis of sacral and lower lumbar vertebrae
Hypoplastic pelvis with narrow hips and flexion contractures
Neurogenic bladder and fecal incontinence

right.title: Associated Diabetic Malformations
points: Transposition of the great arteries and VSD
Small left colon syndrome and duodenal atresia
Neural tube defects (anencephaly, spina bifida)

steps.tx: Metabolic evaluation in stressed or diabetic neonates frequently reveals **early onset neonatal hypocalcaemia**, defined as total serum calcium below seven milligrams per deciliter or ionized calcium under four milligrams per deciliter within seventy-two hours of birth. Clinical signs include exaggerated jitteriness, neuromuscular irritability, high-pitched crying, and prolonged QTc intervals on electrocardiography.
steps.say: Total calcium under seven milligrams per deciliter causes neuromuscular excitability and prolonged QTc intervals.

rows: End of first week of life

steps.tx: Mechanical traction during difficult deliveries with shoulder dystocia causes **Erb Duchenne brachial plexus palsy**, involving the fifth and sixth cervical nerve roots. The classic waiter's tip deformity presents with an adducted, internally rotated shoulder, extended elbow, and pronated forearm. The grasp reflex remains fully intact, while the ipsilateral biceps jerk and Moro reflex are absent.
steps.say: Erb palsy affects C5-C6 roots, producing an internally rotated arm with an intact grasp reflex.

left.title: Erb Palsy (Upper Trunk C5-C6)
points: Shoulder adducted and internally rotated
Elbow extended, forearm pronated ('waiter's tip')
Biceps jerk absent, palmar grasp intact

right.title: Klumpke Palsy (Lower Trunk C8-T1)
points: Intrinsic hand muscle paralysis ('claw hand')
Absent palmar grasp reflex
Associated Horner syndrome if sympathetic T1 root torn
